# Paper Implementation {.unnumbered}

This page is for the **40-mark paper implementation project**. Students will
choose a paper and reproduce a carefully scoped part of its method on a small
or toy dataset. Candidate papers and project specifications will be added here
as they are selected. The grading component is separate from the three
homeworks and the 10-mark mini coding project.

Selection instructions, submission requirements, evaluation criteria, and the
deadline will be announced here and on the [Assignments](./assignments.qmd)
page.

## What each project entry will include

- **Reference:** title, authors, and a link to the paper.
- **Core idea:** the result or algorithm to understand and implement.
- **Implementation scope:** equations and algorithm steps to reproduce, with
  simplifications stated explicitly.
- **Small-scale experiment:** a toy distribution or small dataset, together
  with an appropriate computational budget.
- **Checks:** baselines, plots, or numerical comparisons that assess whether
  the implementation behaves as expected.

## Interpreting a small-scale implementation

The aim is to reproduce and examine a paper's central mechanism at a tractable
scale. A successful toy experiment does not reproduce the paper's full
benchmark results. Each project will distinguish the original method from the
reduced experiment and state what can reasonably be concluded.

The **Papers** section in the navigation contains separate reading tutorials,
such as [Binomial Diffusion](./tutorials/binomial-diffusion-sohl-dickstein.qmd).
Their presence does not by itself make a paper an implementation-project
choice.
